neighbours.label: Inner pieces of Khorasan / Khurasan ('hor', 'uras') and Sohag ('h'): place names from the Islamic world; other places in those regions stay quiet
fire: Persian poets flourished in Khorasan under the Samanids.
An army from Khurasan marched on Baghdad.
Abu Muslim raised his revolt in Khorasan.
Merv was the capital of Khurasan at that time.
The province of Khorasan lies in eastern Iran.
Many scholars came from Khurasan in that age.
Buses run to Sohag and Aswan every morning.
The governor of Sohag visited the temple.
quiet: Persian poets flourished in Isfahan under the Safavids.
An army from Syria marched on Baghdad.
Abu Muslim raised his sons in Damascus.
Merv was the capital of the region at that time.
The province of Fars lies in southern Iran.
Many scholars came from Cairo in that age.
Buses run to Luxor and Aswan every morning.
The governor of Giza visited the temple.

notes: Card: 'f' x3, 'hor' x2, 'ist' x2, 'ay' x2, 'ور' x2, 'uras', ' Law' of Lawami, 'un' of Sunna. Probe: 'uras' 0.80, 'hor' 0.71, 'h' of Sohag 0.56; France, Leeds, North 0.00-0.03. I did not test whether Isfahan, Cairo or Luxor would fire before registering; they are the near misses.
